production.note: US model years 2010-2015. Start: The Auto Channel's '2010 Chevrolet Camaro SS Review' (autochannel-camaro-ss-2010) and Chevrolet's 2010 Camaro SS material reproduced by Motor1 (chevrolet-camaro-ss-motor1-2009). The 2013 (chevrolet-camaro-brochure-2013) and 2015 (chevrolet-camaro-brochure-2015) Chevrolet brochures list the SS with the LS3/L99. End: Chevrolet's 2016 brochure describes the 2016 car as a 'sixth-generation icon' and 'all-new', with a '6.2L LT1 V8' rated 455 hp (chevrolet-camaro-brochure-2016).

body.note: Chevrolet's 2013 brochure lists the SS as coupe and convertible; the 2015 brochure also lists both (chevrolet-camaro-brochure-2015). The convertible did not exist at launch; no opened page gives its first model year.

configuration.note: '6.2L LS3 V8, aluminum block and heads' (manual); '6.2L L99 V8, aluminum block and heads' (automatic)

displacementL.note: Chevrolet's brochure gives '6.2L' only. 6,162 cc: LSX Magazine's reprint of GM's 2010 specifications, '376/6162' (cu in/cc) (lsxmag-2010-camaro-specs).

aspiration.note: Inferred: no forced induction is mentioned for the LS3/L99.

drivetrain.note: GM's 2010 specifications as printed by LSX Magazine: 'Four-passenger, front-engine, rear-drive coupe'.

transmission.note: '6-speed manual with short-throw shifter' (Tremec TR6060, LS3) and '6-speed automatic with overdrive; includes steering wheel-mounted TAPshift controls' (L99). Both offered from 2010: Chevrolet via Motor1, 'The SS model's new Tremec TR 6060 six-speed manual' and 'The L99 is paired exclusively with a six-speed automatic transmission' (chevrolet-camaro-ss-motor1-2009).

powerHp.note: LS3 with the 6-speed manual (the standard car). Quote (Chevrolet 2013 brochure): "6.2L LS3 V8, aluminum block and heads" ... "426 @ 5900 rpm"; the automatic's L99 is "400 @ 5900 rpm". Chevrolet's 2015 brochure repeats "426 @ 5900 rpm" / "400 @ 5900 rpm" (chevrolet-camaro-brochure-2015), and Chevrolet's launch material reproduced by Motor1 says "The LS3 develops 426 hp (318 kW)" and "Horsepower for the L99 is 400 (298 kilowatts)" (chevrolet-camaro-ss-motor1-2009), so the rating did not change over the run. GM's earliest 2010 specification release, as printed by LSX Magazine, gave 422 hp for the LS3 (lsxmag-2010-camaro-specs); see discrepancies.

weightLb.note: Coupe with the 6-speed manual, 2013 model year. Quote (Chevrolet 2013 brochure): "3,849 lbs. (manual Coupe); 3,902 (automatic Coupe)". No Chevrolet figure for the 2010 launch year could be opened (GM's media site blocks access, and auto-brochures.com has no 2010-2011 brochure; the 2012 brochure could not be loaded), so the reference year is 2013. Chevrolet's 2015 brochure gives 3,908 lb manual and 3,946 lb automatic (chevrolet-camaro-brochure-2015). The Auto Channel's 2010 review prints 'Curb weight: 3,849 lbs.' (autochannel-camaro-ss-2010). See discrepancies. LSX Magazine's reprint headed 'OFFICIAL 2010 Camaro Specifications Fully Released by GM' gives 'SS manual: 3860/1755' alongside the preliminary 422 hp rating, so it is treated as a preliminary GM figure and not used for a 2010 reference year.

sources.title: OFFICIAL 2010 Camaro Specifications Fully Released by GM
2010 Chevrolet Camaro SS Review & Test Drive

discrepancies.reason: Model year and preliminary data. 3,849 lb is Chevrolet's 2013 brochure figure for the manual coupe. 3,860 lb ('3860/1755 - SS w/manual') is GM's early 2010 specification release as printed by LSX Magazine, which also still gave the preliminary 422 hp; Automotive Addicts' 2010 review also prints 'Curb Weight: 3860 lbs.' (automotiveaddicts-camaro-ss-2010). 3,908 lb is Chevrolet's 2015 brochure figure after the 2014 restyle.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Chevrolet's own 3,849 lb for the 2013 reference year. The Auto Channel's 2010 review prints the same 3,849 lb.

discrepancies.reason: Preliminary rating. GM's early 2010 specifications gave the LS3 422 hp; Chevrolet's launch material and every later brochure give 426 hp.
